newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran sentences exile in absentia to 10 years jail.
newsitem.headline: Iran sentences exile in absentia to 10 years jail.

text.p: A court in Tehran handed down a 10-year jail sentence for forgery against an Iranian exile who implicated Iran in a anti-Jewish bombing in Argentina in 1994, the official news agency IRNA said on Tuesday.

IRNA said the court convicted Manouchehr Motamer in absentia of forging state documents and also ordered the seizure of 50 million rials ($16,700) that it said he had earned from the forgeries. The report did not say when the sentence was passed.

Motamer, an asylum-seeker who claimed to be a former official, told authorities in Argentina in 1994 he had information linking Iran to the bombing of a Jewish community centre in Buenos Aires which killed 86 people.
An Argentine judge accused Iran of involvement in the case but the charges were later withdrawn for lack of evidence.
Iran strongly denied the charges and said Motamer was an impostor sought by a Tehran court for fraud, forgery and paying bribes.

Motamer later moved to the United States where he told a Persian-language Los Angeles radio station in 1995 that he had seen missing Israeli airman Ron Arad alive in an Iranian jail 11 months earlier.
Iran has repeatedly denied holding Arad who has been missing since his plane was shot down over Lebanon in 1986. ($1 = 3,000 rials at the official exchange rate)
